description: We’re a team of Computer Engineering students from Cameroon, passionate about AI and data, and driven by the search for meaningful, enriching experiences. We’re taking on the Be an Earth Detective challenge to turn satellite data into real environmental insight — combining rigorous engineering with curiosity about how machine learning can help us read our planet.
summary:
TerraSense is an AI-powered Earth observation workstation that combines NASA satellite datasets with subsurface soil profiles to map mineral potential, optimize agriculture, and anticipate climate risks across all 10 regions of Cameroon, and in perspective extensible to other zones of the world.
To eliminate the technical barrier of geospatial data, our platform features a bilingual semantic AI engine (French/English) that understands complex natural-language queries with a 90.4% detection rate. Users simply ask a question in plain language without technical jargon; the system automatically identifies the target region, filters out negative constraints, and selects at most 5 relevant variables from 11 indicators spanning NASA Giovanni (GLDAS, MODIS), continuous climate series (2003–2026), and SoilGrids subsurface profiles (0–200 cm).
Beyond variable selection, the platform computes real-time long-term environmental trends over more than two decades using robust Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen statistical estimators rendered on an interactive 3D globe. This end-to-end workflow identifies geological alteration zones favorable to mineral deposits (bauxite, iron, gold) via deep clay and soil acidity, recommends fertile farmland, and tracks evolving flood risks (Douala) or Sahelian droughts (Maroua).
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TerraSense Cameroon eliminates the technical barrier of complex geospatial data through a three-stage workflow:


• Bilingual Semantic Routing: Users ask a question in plain English or French without technical jargon. A custom fine-tuned neural network (paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2) combined with a neuro-symbolic inference engine identifies the target Cameroonian city or region, filters out negative constraints, and selects at most 5 relevant indicators from 11 variables (90.4% Recall@5).
• Multi-Source Data Fusion: The backend cross-references continuous climate series (2003–2026: rainfall, surface and root-zone soil moisture, soil temperature, evapotranspiration), NASA Giovanni archives (GLDAS surface runoff, MODIS aerosol optical depth), and SoilGrids subsurface profiles (0–200 cm: clay, nitrogen, organic carbon, pH).
• Real-Time Trend Analysis & 3D Visualization: Using non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen statistical estimators, the platform computes long-term environmental trends and renders interactive time series and subsurface depth profiles on a full-screen 3D globe.

What benefits does it have?

• Zero Technical Barrier: Farmers, miners, and urban planners do not need to know satellite sensor names or manipulate raw NetCDF/CSV files.
• High Precision & Noise Rejection: Unlike standard keyword searches, our negative-intent filter prevents false positives when users explicitly exclude certain phenomena.
• Nationwide Generalization: Although trained on three contrasting climatic zones (coastal Douala, central Yaoundé, and Sahelian Maroua), the physical and semantic logic generalizes seamlessly across all 10 regions of Cameroon as soon as regional datasets are loaded.

What is the intended impact of the project?

• Precision Agriculture & Food Security: Recommends optimal farmlands by scoring root-zone water reserves and soil nutrient fertility (nitrogen, organic carbon, pH).
• Geological & Mineral Prospecting: Identifies subsurface alteration zones favorable to bauxite (Adamawa), iron, and alluvial gold (East and South) by analyzing deep clay layers (0–200 cm), chemical acidity, and surface erosion.
• Climate & Urban Risk Mitigation: Helps local authorities anticipate urban flooding caused by clay soil saturation in coastal cities like Douala and monitor deep soil drying or Harmattan dust in northern regions.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

• AI and Data Science: Python, PyTorch, Sentence-Transformers (TripletLoss fine-tuning), NumPy, Pandas, and SciPy/Scikit-learn (Mann-Kendall and Theil-Sen trend estimators).
• Backend and Frontend: FastAPI (Uvicorn) REST API, TypeScript/JavaScript, Vite, CesiumJS, and Google Maps Photorealistic 3D Tiles.
• Datasets: NASA Giovanni (GLDAS Noah v2.0/v2.1, MODIS Terra/Aqua MYD08), ISRIC SoilGrids (0–200 cm), and regional continuous climate series (2003–2026).
• Hardware: Cloud NVIDIA T4 GPU (Google Colab) for neural model fine-tuning and standard CPU workstations for local inference and 3D rendering.

How is your project creative?

• Neuro-Symbolic Architecture: Instead of relying purely on black-box embeddings, we paired a multilingual Transformer with deterministic physical rules—preventing duplicate sensor versions, enforcing strict negative-intent exclusions, and mapping local neighborhoods (such as Bonabéri or Bafia) to regional satellite bounding boxes.
• Subsurface-to-Space Synergy: Combining 20+ years of atmospheric/surface satellite trends with 2-meter underground soil profiles bridges agriculture, hydrology, and mineral exploration in a single interface.

What factors did your team consider?


• Linguistic and Domain Accessibility: Cameroon is bilingual (French and English) with diverse local place names; our model handles mixed-language queries and translates everyday symptoms into scientific parameters.
• Data Continuity and Integrity: We prioritized continuous datasets up to 2026 for current trend analysis while filtering out coastal/marine null points in SoilGrids and missing-value flags (-9999) in NASA Giovanni archives.
• Cognitive Load: Limiting output to at most 5 variables ensures clear, actionable visual diagnostics without overwhelming decision-makers.
